state.draft: keep the reader where they chose to read
recordTexts: Start with the work. A review should make the next step easier to see.
Keep the labels close to the controls. There is no need to make someone remember them.
The narrow layout feels calmer when the transcript gets its own scrolling space.
Use a real button to return to the latest entry. It should say what it does.
When someone selects a sentence, they are telling us they are reading. Leave that sentence where it is.
New entries can wait. An unread count is more useful than pulling the reader away.
A growing paragraph is still one record. Let the host declare the actual new-record count.
Keep the glass around the controls, and keep the long-form text on a quiet surface.
For keyboard users, returning to the end should not steal focus from the button or the draft.
Give people a place to stop. A useful feed does not have to keep moving.
